summary.headline: Physicswallah Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR1,242 crores, a record, with Pre-Ind AS EBITDA of INR233 crores at an 18.8% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,242 crores (+18% YoY), with online up 26% to INR694 crores and offline up 9% to INR541 crores. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 45% to INR233 crores (18.8% margin, +350 bps), and PAT was INR142 crores versus INR70 crores a year earlier, taking H1 PAT to INR55 crores from a loss. NEET demand, delayed by a month, recovered only partly in Q2, and government-exam enrollments fell 24%, which weighed on offline and subsidiary Xylem. Management kept full-year consolidated revenue guidance of around 30% and said M&A is included in that figure. The company also sold its FinZ loan book and acquired an 11% stake in Sarrthi IAS.

financial_highlights.value: INR5,268 crores, including INR1,800 crores IPO proceeds

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR694 crores (+26%); H1 online growth 29%, core online 34%. Unique transacting users rose to 3.44 million from 3.22 million; ACPU up 9.2% to INR4,280.

segments.name: Offline
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR541 crores (+9%); H1 collections growth around 11%. Vidyapeeth contributed 66% of H1 offline revenue, with 167 centres against 117 a year ago. Utkarsh Classes was hit by government-exam notification delays.

segments.name: Xylem (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 80% of its business depends on NEET, so it was hit hardest by the delayed NEET cycle. Management is working on diversifying its categories.

segments.name: Categories beyond JEE/NEET
segments.commentary: Contributed 73.8% of H1 enrollments, up from 64.8%. K-12 collections grew about 49%. Skills and Earners grew 10x. Finance (CA, CS, ACCA, CFA) grew about 30%. Boards and CUET enrollments rose 130%.

segments.name: FinZ (NBFC)
segments.commentary: Sold its entire INR96 crore loan book to Auxilo Finserve on 3 Oct 2026. Student lending moves to third-party NBFCs; FinZ will close subject to RBI approval.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated FY27 revenue growth guidance of around 30% reaffirmed; management said there is no change and that M&A is included in this figure.
Group Pre-Ind AS EBITDA growth of about 100% targeted for FY27, mostly from online.
PAT expected to be positive for the full year (H1 PAT already INR55 crores).
Offline expected to move to near break-even this year (management referenced about -12% margin); Vidyapeeth expected to turn EBITDA positive this year.
Management said it was too early to say whether growth would exceed 30%. Mega crash courses for NEET are planned for Q3 and Q4 in online and offline.
M&A contribution to FY27 guidance is expected to be less than 5%; about USD20 million is earmarked for online acquisitions out of the INR1,800 crore IPO proceeds to be deployed over two years.
capex_capacity: Offline centre expansion slowed; plan is about 25-30 Vidyapeeth centres opened per year over the next two to three years, plus government-exam offline centres. Last year about 50 Vidyapeeth centres were opened.
Vidyapeeth count rose to 167 from 117 a year ago; 370 offline centres in total.

PW Digital University (PWDU) notified in the Punjab Government Gazette effective 29 Oct 2026; admissions expected from July 2027, and a business plan will be shared in the next 3-6 months. Management described it as capital-light.
Sarrthi IAS: acquired 11% for INR71 crores, consummated in Q2; the company says it is now the largest civil services educator in India.
Socratic AI tutor (PW AI Tuto) is live with about 4,000 students and 5,000+ learning hours; paid launch timed with Vishwas Diwas. Live AI translation covers 12 Indic languages, targeting 20.
demand_pricing: NEET online collections rose 27% and enrollments over 30% in Q2, but full-cycle online NEET collections are still 7% below last year and enrollments 13% lower. Offline NEET enrollments for the academic year are 8% lower.
Government-exam enrollments fell 24% on delayed notifications and vacancies.
Q2 unique enrollments rose 12.9% to 1.5 million; ACPU up 9.2% to INR4,280. Infinity Pro collections rose 32%, lifting share to 35% from 31%.
Offline ARPU growth of about 5-7%, which management attributed to mix shift toward new centres; Vidyapeeth ARPU is 9-10% higher YoY.
Collections growth was about 16-17% in H1 versus 24% in Q1, per analyst questions. Management expects collections to flow into Q3 and beyond.
NEET is only about 15% of online revenue. Skills enrollments rose 10.3x to 1.69 lakh; CA enrollments rose 19%; NEET PG enrollments rose 35% to 9,500.

qa_highlights.question: Given NEET's partial recovery, how much must collection growth accelerate for the 30% full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 NEET collections and enrollments improved significantly, with some collections spilling into Q3. It relies on mega crash courses, Earners, PW Talk/Books/Pi (INR3-4 million uplift) and newer categories such as CA and CLAT. It stated it is confident of the annual guidance but could not quantify how much of the NEET gap would be covered.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a chance online growth ends above 30% given the H2 crash courses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was too early to say and did not want to guide above 30%. Internal online targets have been exceeded, and K-12 is beating its annual operating plan. The 360-degree tracker product is being extended from JEE to NEET.

qa_highlights.question: Will online EBITDA margins (about 35%) be reinvested in marketing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to shift margins into marketing. Online margins may rise in the next two to three years, but spending is currently going into AI tutor development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to consolidated revenue guidance despite the offline shortfall? Is M&A included?
qa_highlights.answer: No change. Online is compensating for offline, and the majority of the offline hit came from NEET and government exams. The guidance includes M&A; the company is in advanced talks on a couple of online assets, and M&A is expected to contribute under 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics and pricing for AI Tuto?
qa_highlights.answer: Price discovery has not happened yet. The indicative price is about 2x online ACPU. Cost is below INR20 per hour of tutoring, and paid monetisation this year will be minimal. The first launch targets grades 6-12 and JEE/NEET.

qa_highlights.question: Will offline break even this year given H1 EBITDA loss of about INR108 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 and Q3 are the strongest offline quarters. H2 expansion costs are much lower because Vidyapeeth openings were slowed. Vidyapeeth is expected to break even or be profitable this year, and subsidiary cost cuts are underway.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and faculty counts fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to AI efficiencies in content, QC, test-paper making and subjective-answer evaluation. Employee count is about 19,100 and faculty about 7,100.

risks_watch: NEET remains structurally behind: online NEET collections are 7% below last year on a full-cycle basis, and offline NEET enrollments are 8% lower.
Xylem's 80% NEET dependence and Utkarsh's exposure to government-exam notifications both weigh on offline; the timing of the government-exam notifications is outside management's control.
The 30% FY27 revenue guidance depends on H2 collections, crash-course results and M&A (guided at under 5% contribution); the deals are not yet announced.
Offline break-even (near break-even, about -12% margin) and Vidyapeeth EBITDA break-even need to be confirmed in H2.
Tuto/AI monetisation is unproven; paid launch is timed with the academic cycle. Investor Day on 18 Nov 2026 is the next checkpoint.
The FinZ wind-down is subject to RBI approval. Management says PWDU's business plan will come in the next 3-6 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers and the full-year targets, with the record Q2 and PAT turnaround emphasised. It was more guarded on NEET recovery and on whether growth will exceed 30%, deferring specifics to crash courses and Investor Day.
key_quotes: This quarter has been amazing for PW. This was a very strong quarter for us.
We are not targeting any M&A growth in southern part of the country.
There is no change in consol revenue guidance at all because the compensation of offline is being done by online.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed ~30% FY27 consolidated revenue growth (including M&A, expected <5% contribution) and ~100% group EBITDA growth, backed by Q2 revenue +18% and Pre-Ind AS EBITDA +45%, online +26%, and Infinity Pro/NEET online demand, but full-cycle NEET collections remain 7% below last year and government-exam enrollments fell 24%, so backing is only partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin rose 350 bps to 18.8% in Q2 and H1 margin 8.3% (+450 bps), with group EBITDA growth of about 100% guided for FY27 mostly from online (online margin 34.4%) and offline moving toward near break-even (about -12% margin).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vidyapeeth centres rose to 167 from 117 a year ago, with about 25-30 new centres per year planned over the next 2-3 years versus about 50 last year, so capacity grows but at a slower pace.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 online revenue rose 26% with unique transacting users up to 3.44 million from 3.22 million and H1 core online growth at 34%, though full-cycle NEET collections are still 7% below last year and government-exam enrollments fell 24%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Offline expansion has slowed to about 25-30 Vidyapeeth centres per year, PWDU is described as capital-light, and utilisation was not discussed, so no major new capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 consolidated revenue growth at about 30% and said it was too early to say whether growth would exceed 30%, and did not want to guide above it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 30% guide depends on H2 collections and crash courses after NEET full-cycle collections ran 7% below last year, government-exam enrollments fell 24%, and M&A (under 5% of guidance) is not yet announced.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Mega NEET crash courses are planned for Q3 and Q4, PW AI Tuto is live with about 4,000 students and a paid launch is timed with the academic cycle, and PWDU admissions are expected from July 2027.

rows.label: Mega NEET crash courses in Q3-Q4 to recover NEET gap
rows.why: NEET online enrollments are down 13% and full-cycle collections 7% below last year, and management is relying on the crash courses plus Earners and CA/CLAT categories to close the gap to the 30% guide.

rows.label: FinZ loan book sale and wind-down
rows.why: The INR96 crore loan book was sold to Auxilo Finserve on 3 Oct 2026, with FinZ closing subject to RBI approval.

rows.label: Online M&A (advanced talks; USD20m earmarked)
rows.why: Management is in advanced talks on a couple of online assets, with M&A contributing under 5% of FY27 guidance and about USD20 million of the INR1,800 crore IPO proceeds earmarked for online acquisitions.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record Q2, PAT turnaround and the held 30% and 100% EBITDA guides, but guarded on NEET recovery and on whether growth would exceed 30%; analysts pressed on how much collections must accelerate and on offline break-even.
